case_study_insert.main_stem: Apex Mobile Applications (APX) is a partnership in the mobile app development sector, employing a workforce of 40 across its product teams. Founded in 2015 by Marcus Bell, it designs productivity apps for small businesses and operates a hierarchical structure with democratic leadership that consults developers before each release. APX plans to invest $680,000 in a new app-testing laboratory with automated crash-reporting, financed by $400,000 hire purchase and $280,000 retained profit. It has fixed costs of $300,000 a year, a variable cost of $12.00 a unit and a selling price of $27.00, and currently produces 60,000 units a year. APX faces two problems: a 1.9% app crash rate after updates and 12 of 40 staff lacking mobile-security training.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: App Performance Report — Q3 2025: APX released 9,600 app updates; the crash rate was 1.9%, down from 3.6% a year earlier, and user ratings averaged 4.2 out of 5. Daily active users rose from 42,000 to 58,000. A survey of 500 users found 71% value offline access and 63% would recommend the app. A skills audit shows 12 of 40 staff lack mobile-security training; a certification course costs $880 per employee.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Profit or Loss and Capital employed data of Apex Mobile Applications for the year ended 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Digital Bulletin (July 2026): (1) The base interest rate rose from 3.5% to 4.25%, increasing the cost of variable-rate finance agreements. (2) The national minimum wage increased by 6.4% to $13.10 an hour from April 2026. (3) Cloud hosting and developer-tool input costs rose 8.9% year-on-year, while consumer app spending grew 4.8%.

questions.question_text: APX plans to acquire part of its $680,000 app-testing laboratory through hire purchase. Explain two advantages for APX of using retained profit instead of hire purchase.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Retained profit carries no hire-purchase interest or instalments, so APX can commit the $280,000 to the $680,000 laboratory without adding to fixed costs of $300,000 a year or to the $400,000 hire-purchase commitment. Cash saved can fund certification at $880 per employee for the 12 untrained staff and help reduce the 1.9% crash rate, protecting the $27.00 price.

Point 2: Using internal funds avoids the risk that the lab equipment is repossessed if repayments are missed, unlike hire purchase where ownership passes only at the end. It also preserves the partnership's decision-making independence, letting Marcus Bell change testing priorities as the 500-user survey (71% wanting offline access) evolves, without a finance company's conditions. Retained profit is therefore cheaper and lower-risk than hire purchase. With consumer app spending growing 4.8%, that freed cash can fund features the 71% of surveyed users want, such as offline access, rather than payments to a finance company.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation and analysis applied to APX's financing decision, costs and laboratory investment.

questions.question_text: APX is promoting a new productivity app. Consider social media influencer campaigns, paid search advertising, or in-app referral rewards. Which should APX choose to promote the launch? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Social media influencer campaigns: Influencers can demonstrate the app to large, targeted audiences quickly and make the 71% of surveyed users who value offline access aware of the feature. Costs vary widely and results depend on influencer credibility, with little control over the message; for a 40-person partnership spending $680,000 on a testing lab, a large campaign would be risky.

Paid search advertising: Ads shown to people searching for productivity apps give measurable clicks and can emphasise a 4.2 out of 5 rating and offline access. However, keyword costs rise with competition and require continuous optimisation, a skill APX lacks while 12 of 40 staff need mobile-security training, so spend could be wasted.

In-app referral rewards: Offering existing users a small reward for recommendations uses the 58,000 daily active users and the 63% who would already recommend the app. It is low-cost, self-targeting and measurable through downloads, though rewards reduce revenue per unit on a $27.00 price and growth is gradual.

Recommendation: APX should choose in-app referral rewards. They harness the 63% willing to recommend among 500 surveyed users and the 42,000-to-58,000 growth in active users, at low cost that can be funded from $280,000 retained profit rather than more hire purchase. Influencer campaigns are rejected as unpredictable and costly; paid search is rejected because competitive keywords and a skills gap would waste cash that is needed to cover $300,000 fixed costs. Referrals also fit a hierarchical structure where Marcus Bell can reward users quickly without a complex campaign approval chain.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Lists or describes promotional options with limited application to APX.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Discusses advantages and disadvantages of at least two options in APX's context with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Evaluates all three options in APX's context and gives a justified recommendation explaining why influencer campaigns and paid search are rejected.

questions.question_text: APX has a 1.9% crash rate and 12 of its 40 staff lack mobile-security training. Explain two benefits for APX of using democratic leadership in its development teams.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Democratic leadership invites developers to help set release and testing routines, so staff who see crashes first can suggest fixes. Their involvement raises ownership (Maslow's esteem needs) and targets the 1.9% crash rate and 4.2 out of 5 rating, which matter to the 63% of users who recommend the app. In a hierarchical structure, consultation gives Marcus Bell practical information before the $680,000 laboratory changes workflows.

Point 2: Involving the team in decisions about the $880 certification courses helps close the mobile-security gap among 12 of 40 staff because developers can identify their own training needs and are more willing to attend. Participation raises commitment, reducing disruption in a 40-person workforce where 60,000 units must be maintained, and generates ideas for the 71% of users who want offline access. Shared decisions also suit a partnership culture. This involvement also helps when the 71% of users who want offline access suggest features that developers must then build.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to APX's crash rate, skills gap and laboratory investment.

questions.question_text: APX must address the mobile-security training gap among 12 staff. Consider on-the-job coaching or external certification at $880 per employee. Which should APX choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
On-the-job coaching: Coaching during releases is specific to APX's own app and testing lab, requires no fees and keeps all 12 staff producing the 60,000 units while they learn, helping maintain the 4.2 out of 5 rating and reduce the 1.9% crash rate. Developers can demonstrate the exact security checks users expect. However, the trainers may lack formal certification themselves, bad habits can be copied, and no qualification is awarded, which is a weakness when 71% of surveyed users value offline data security.

External certification: An accredited course gives recognised, current security skills and a qualification that supports APX's reputation. For 12 staff the fee is 12 × $880 = $10,560, an explicit calculation from the insert, affordable against $280,000 retained profit. Staff are away from releases temporarily and generic content may not match APX's app, so follow-up coaching on the new lab would still be needed.

Decision: APX should choose external certification. The $10,560 cost is modest against the $680,000 investment, the qualification is credible with users, and on-the-job coaching cannot certify 12 untrained staff. On-the-job coaching is rejected because APX's own trainers may not be qualified and a 1.9% crash rate leaves little room for errors while the new laboratory is being introduced. A certification also helps the partnership compete for skilled developers when IT salary inflation and a 1.9% crash rate make mistakes costly. The $10,560 is a single payment from retained profit, and sending the 12 staff in two groups would keep release schedules intact while the new crash-reporting lab is commissioned.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of the two training methods with limited application to APX.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed analysis of benefits and drawbacks of both methods in APX's context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both methods with a justified decision covering cost, credibility and release disruption, rejecting the alternative.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how APX's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $300,000 ÷ ($27.00 − $12.00) = $300,000 ÷ $15.00 = 20,000 units. Answer: break-even output is 20,000 units a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $27.00 − $12.00 = $15.00. Answer: contribution per unit is $15.00.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways APX's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Compare the 20,000-unit break-even output with 60,000 units actually released to show a margin of safety of 40,000 units, indicating how far demand can fall before the $680,000 laboratory fails to cover costs.
2. Use $15.00 contribution to model reward costs for the referral scheme: a $1.00 reward leaves $14.00, so managers can calculate the extra downloads required to keep covering $300,000 fixed costs.
3. Check that 60,000 × $15.00 = $900,000 contribution covers $300,000 fixed costs and the $400,000 hire-purchase commitment, informing partner decisions on further borrowing.
4. Benchmark unit cost ($300,000 ÷ 60,000 = $5.00 plus $12.00 = $17.00 a unit, with labour productivity of 60,000 ÷ 40 = 1,500 units per employee) to spot the 8.9% developer-tool inflation and link costs to the 1.9% crash rate.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 20,000 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $15.00 | (iii) Four contextual uses explained: margin of safety of 40,000 units against 60,000-unit output; referral-reward modelling with $300,000 fixed costs; hire-purchase feasibility on the $400,000 agreement; and unit-cost benchmarking at $17.00 with 1,500-unit productivity.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method, 1 mark for accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii). 1 mark per valid applied point in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate APX's profitability by calculating the gross profit margin, profit margin and return on capital employed for 2024 and 2025. Has APX's profitability improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Gross Profit Margin 2024 = 50.0%
Gross Profit Margin 2025 = 54.0%
Profit Margin 2024 = 20.0%
Profit Margin 2025 = 24.0%
ROCE 2024 = 15.0%
ROCE 2025 = 20.0%

Detailed workings: 2024 gross profit $600 ÷ revenue $1,200 = 50.0%; 2025 gross profit $810 ÷ revenue $1,500 = 54.0%. Operating profit 2024 $240 ÷ revenue $1,200 = 20.0%; 2025 $360 ÷ revenue $1,500 = 24.0%. Operating profit 2024 $240 ÷ capital employed $1,600 = 15.0%; 2025 $360 ÷ capital employed $1,800 = 20.0%. Revenue grew from $1,200 to $1,500 while cost of sales rose only from $600 to $690, so gross profit increased faster than sales.

Evaluation: Profitability improved strongly. The higher gross percentage shows better control of direct development costs relative to revenue, consistent with a $27.00 price and $12.00 variable cost on 60,000 units. The operating percentage rose from 20.0% to 24.0% because operating profit grew from $240 to $360 more quickly than revenue, showing $300,000 fixed costs were spread over more apps. The return on capital rose from 15.0% to 20.0%, meaning the larger $1,800 capital base is being used more productively, which supports the $680,000 laboratory. Interest payable rose from $30 to $42 but is small against $360 operating profit.

Conclusion: APX's profitability has improved: all three measures increased together and the gain is driven by revenue growth and cost control rather than by reducing capital. The caution is that variable-rate hire purchase and a 1.9% crash rate could erode the 54.0% gross percentage, so the partnership should protect quality while expanding.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates the gross profit margin, profit margin and ROCE for both years with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate calculations for both years combined with detailed evaluation of revenue, cost and capital movements and a justified conclusion on profitability.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for APX of introducing automated crash-reporting in its app development.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Automated crash-reporting identifies faults as soon as they appear, directly attacking the 1.9% crash rate and supporting the 4.2 out of 5 rating. Fewer crashes protect the 63% of surveyed users who recommend the app and the 58,000 daily active users, sustaining the $27.00 price and $15.00 contribution on 60,000 units and helping justify the $680,000 laboratory.

Disadvantage: The reporting system is part of the $680,000 investment and could raise the $300,000 fixed costs, lifting the 20,000-unit break-even output. It also depends on skills that 12 of 40 staff lack, so misread alerts or alert fatigue could distract developers and slow releases, especially while the new hire-purchase equipment is being installed. APX can evaluate the tool against the 9,600 updates released last quarter and the 4.2 out of 5 rating, so any improvement in crash rate is measurable. This matters because the 500-user survey shows users are quick to recommend or reject an app on reliability.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to APX's crash rate, user data, costs and skills.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the interest rate rise to 4.25%, the 6.4% minimum wage increase to $13.10 and the 8.9% rise in cloud hosting and developer-tool costs will affect APX. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (3.5% to 4.25%): If the $400,000 hire-purchase agreement is linked to the base rate, the additional cost is 0.75% × $400,000 = $3,000 a year (0.0075 × $400,000). That is small next to $300,000 fixed costs and $360 of operating profit, and the $280,000 retained profit reduces dependence on finance. Future agreements may cost more, but the direct annual effect is limited.

Minimum wage increase (6.4% to $13.10): The insert gives a workforce of 40 but no hours worked or number of low-paid staff, so an annual wage bill cannot be invented. The proper judgement is qualitative: a 6.4% rise pushes up unit labour cost unless productivity holds at 60,000 ÷ 40 = 1,500 units per employee, and the mobile-security gap among 12 staff makes that harder. It does improve the relative value of the $880 certification course.

Cloud hosting and developer-tool inflation (8.9%): The insert gives a variable cost of $12.00 a unit without decomposing it. A labelled upper bound if the full variable cost rose 8.9% is 0.089 × $12.00 = $1.068 a unit; across 60,000 units that is 60,000 × $1.068 = $64,080 a year, reducing contribution from $15.00 to $13.93. Even partial pass-through would narrow the surplus covering $300,000 fixed costs.

Conclusion: The 8.9% rise in hosting and developer-tool costs will have the greatest impact. It applies to every unit, can add $64,080 a year on the stated assumption and directly erodes the $15.00 contribution that funds the $680,000 laboratory; the interest rise is at most $3,000 and the wage effect cannot be quantified from the insert and can be offset by maintaining 1,500-unit productivity.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external changes with limited application to APX.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two external changes on APX's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three changes in APX's context with justified greatest-impact judgement and shown derivations, rejecting the smaller effects.
